_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: This skill provides prioritization frameworks for AI engineering: RICE-A (adding AI Ambiguity to RICE) for product…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "This skill provides prioritization frameworks for AI engineering: RICE-A (adding AI Ambiguity to RICE) for product features, ICE for research experiments, and MoSCoW for MVP/Release scoping. Use when ranking the backlog, deciding which model research path to…"
cases.context: The agent has access to the prioritization skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is prioritization the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes prioritization as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against constraint-awareness, bayesian-reasoning, playing-to-win
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the prioritization workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore prioritization
Does not route to constraint-awareness, bayesian-reasoning, playing-to-win when the prioritization scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence

cases.scenario: A user asks for work that is near prioritization but is explicitly outside its declared scope.
cases.context: This is a boundary test. The skill should avoid false-positive activation and route to the better owner when appropriate.
cases.question: Should prioritization be applied here? If not, what should happen instead?
expected_flags: Recognizes the request is outside prioritization's ownership
Routes the work to constraint-awareness or asks for the missing owner instead of forcing this skill
Preserves any real issue in the request without applying prioritization terminology incorrectly
expected_fix_hints: Decline to apply prioritization as the primary skill
Name the better owner or the boundary reason
Offer only a narrow handoff if prioritization has a secondary support role
absent_signals: Does not claim prioritization should own the request
Does not use prioritization's framework to solve an explicitly excluded problem
Does not suppress the correct adjacent owner
